You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE conductor (
    Conductor_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    Nationality TEXT,
    Year_of_Work INT,
    UNIQUE (Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE orchestra (
    Orchestra_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra TEXT,
    Conductor_ID INT,
    Record_Company TEXT,
    Year_of_Founded REAL,
    Major_Record_Format TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Orchestra_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Conductor_ID) REFERENCES conductor(Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE performance (
    Performance_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra_ID INT,
    Type TEXT,
    Date TEXT,
    Official_ratings_(millions) REAL,
    Weekly_rank TEXT,
    Share TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Performance_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Orchestra_ID) REFERENCES orchestra(Orchestra_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE show (
    Show_ID INT,
    Performance_ID INT,
    If_first_show bool,
    Result TEXT,
    Attendance REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Performance_ID) REFERENCES performance(Performance_ID)
);

“Famous” isn’t a field in your schema, so we need a proxy (e.g., conductors whose orchestras have the highest ratings/attendance, or most performances).

Here are a few useful SQL options—pick the one that matches what you mean:

### 1) Conductors with highest total official ratings (proxy for fame)
```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  SUM(p."Official_ratings_(millions)") AS total_ratings_millions
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY total_ratings_millions DESC;
```

### 2) Conductors with most performances
```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS performance_count
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY performance_count DESC;
```

### 3) Conductors with highest total attendance (from shows)
```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  SUM(s.Attendance) AS total_attendance
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
JOIN show s ON s.Performance_ID = p.Performance_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY total_attendance DESC;
```

Which definition of “famous” do you want (ratings, attendance, number of performances, or something else like top weekly rank)?
Only include conductors who have led multiple orchestras, not just one.

```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) AS orchestras_led
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) > 1
ORDER BY orchestras_led DESC, c.Name;
```

If you want “famous” using a proxy (e.g., highest total ratings) *but only among those conductors*, tell me which proxy to use.
Only want conductors who led multiple orchestras. Make sure that's included.

```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) AS orchestras_led
FROM conductor AS c
JOIN orchestra AS o
  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
GROUP BY
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) > 1
ORDER BY
  orchestras_led DESC,
  c.Name;
```
Only consider conductors based on their past conducting activities.

Assuming “past conducting activities” means **conductors who have actually conducted performances** (i.e., have performance records), and still **only those who led multiple orchestras**, use:

```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) AS orchestras_led,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.Performance_ID) AS past_performances
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o
  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p
  ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) > 1
ORDER BY past_performances DESC, orchestras_led DESC, c.Name;
```

If “past” should exclude future-dated `performance.Date`, tell me the date format in that column (e.g., `YYYY-MM-DD`).
